SUPREMACY OF RULES: This procurement is executed on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) platfo rm. The contract shall be primarily governed by the GeM General Terms and Conditions (GTC), Product Spe cific Terms and Conditions (STC), and the digitally generated GeM Bid Document. For all matters, legal prot ections, and operational procedures where the GeM GTC/STC remains silent, ambiguous, or does not provi de specific functional modules, the guidelines and provisions of the Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 20 25 shall apply as a supplemental framework. 2. FALLBACK MECHANISM: Defence-specific requirements—including but not limited to the Risk & Expen se Clause, MoD-specific Bilateral Arbitration, Quality Assurance protocols, and Local Board of Officers Post- Dispatch Inspection—stipulated in this ATC document shall remain fully valid, enforceable, and binding fall back mechanisms upon the Seller. 3. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: All items supplied under this contract must strictly conform to the tech nical and physical parameters defined in Indian Air Force Specification IAFS 02017 May 2024. Supply of su b-standard, commercial-grade, or noncompliant substitutes will result in summary rejection of the entire c onsignment. 4. TENDER SAMPLE SUBMISSION: All participating bidders must submit a sample matching the exact p arameters of IAFS 02017 (May 2024) to the Buyer's designated facility on or before the bid opening date a nd time. Submitted samples will be thoroughly evaluated at the Buyer's end using specialized tools, weigh

t matrices, and testing equipment for verification of core Quality Assurance parameters as per IAFS 02017 May 24. 5. MATERIAL TEST REPORT: Bidders are mandatory required to upload a valid, authentic material test r eport from a National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) approved laborat ory along with their online bid submission. The test report must explicitly substantiate compliance with the fabric composition, tensile strength, and weave parameters set out in specification IAFS 02017 May 24. 6. BIDDER'S MANUFACTURING CAPACITY: To ensure delivery capability for a high-volume public order, bidders must upload proof of direct manufacturing capacity. This must include a valid National Small Indus tries Corporation (NSIC) Certificate or an active Factory License explicitly showing a production capacity. 7. QUALITY MANAGEMENT CERTIFICATIONS: Bidders must submit copies of valid ISO 9001 and ISO OE KO-TEX Standard 100 certification systems. These certifications must explicitly cover the manufacturing of raw, semi-finished, and finished textiles to guarantee eco-friendly and standardized manufacturing baselin es. 8. PACKING, MARKING, AND LABELLING: The packing, marking, and labeling of the product must be ca rried out securely and strictly as per the defense-specific instructions detailed in the bid documents and sp ecification IAFS 02017 May 24. Blankets must be securely bound in weather-proof HDPE/tarpaulin bales co ntaining fixed quantities to prevent environmental degradation during multi-station transit and depot stora ge. 9. CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES: Consequential damages may be legally imposed over and above Liquid ated Damages (LD) in case of time-critical delivery failure or operational shortfalls. The specific valuation fr amework for consequential damages shall be explicitly finalized and appended by the Buyer during the for mal placement of the contract/sanction. 10. ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION: All disputes shall be settled conclusively through the bi lateral arbitration mechanism as defined in Part 3 of the Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 2025 (DPMF- 11 format). The designated appointing authority for the sole arbitrator shall be the Representative of Head quarters Training Command (HQ TC). Legal proceedings, if any, shall be subject exclusively to military/civil jurisdiction at the location of HQ TC or the Buyer's headquarters. 11. DENIAL CLAUSE (DELIVERY EXTENSIONS): In case of delay in delivery or an extension to the deliv ery period is granted due to delays attributable strictly to the Seller or due to non-Force Majeure events, a ny statutory increase in taxes, fresh imposition of duties/contracts, or any upward rise in prices due to Pric e Variation or adverse foreign exchange fluctuations shall be borne entirely by the Seller during the exten ded delivery period. Conversely, the Buyer reserves the absolute right to claim the benefit of any structura l decrease in prices, taxes, or duties taking place during the said extended period. 12. TOLERANCE CLAUSE: The Buyer reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity of the requir ed goods up to a limit of 15% at the time of final contract placement without any change in the unit prices or other terms and conditions quoted by the bidder. All bidders must explicitly confirm acceptance of this operational framework. 13. RISK & EXPENSE CLAUSE: If the Supplier fails to deliver the blankets within the stipulated delivery p eriod, the Buyer reserves the absolute right to cancel the contract (or any non-delivered portion thereof) vi a the GeM Incident Management Tool. The Buyer shall be entitled to procure identical or similar items from an alternative supplier under a 'Risk & Expense' framework. Any upward financial differential, premium, or extra cost incurred in such an alternative purchase shall be recovered directly from the defaulting Seller's e-PBG (Performance Bank Guarantee) or pending invoices across any government department. 14. EARLIEST ACCEPTABLE YEAR OF MANUFACTURE: To ensure maximum shelf life and material fres hness, all blankets supplied under this order must have been manufactured no earlier than June 2026. Bou nded lots must be completely fresh production. 15. FRANKING CLAUSE: The fact that the goods have been inspected after the original delivery period h as expired and rejected by the inspecting officer will not bind the Buyer in any manner. The goods are bein g inspected and rejected without prejudice to the statutory rights of the Buyer under the terms and conditi ons of the contract, and no automatic legal extension of delivery timeline shall be inferred from such admi nistrative actions. 16. WARRANTY AND DEFECT LIABILITY: If within the period of the warranty, the goods are reported by the Buyer to have failed to perform as per technical specifications, the Seller shall either replace or rectify the same free of charge within a maximum period of 30 days from formal notification of such defect. The r eplacement goods must be fresh, un-used production conforming perfectly to the main contract specificati

ons. 17. RECORDS AND QUALITY AUDIT: The Seller shall maintain detailed production, material traceability, and quality control records necessary to establish compliance with the contract parameters. These record s shall include procurement receipts of raw material and batch inspection logs, which must be kept open f or evaluation and audit by the Buyer's authorized inspectors or CGDA/CDA representatives. 18. PATTERN / SPECIFICATION AMENDMENTS: Where the Competent Technical Authority changes the applicable specifications or patterns during the currency of the contract, the Seller shall comply with the ap proved change in accordance with the revised terms. The formal procedure for treatment of existing stock, work-in-progress, and transition timelines shall be determined solely and specifically by the Buyer. 19. DELIVERY LOCATION: The exact quantity allocation and contact points for distribution are finalized a s per the multi-station matrix detailed below. Actual delivery schedules and specific names of contact offic ers will be formally intimated via official email immediately post-placement of the contract on the GeM por tal: 19.1. ATS SAMBRA, BELAGAVI. 19.2. AFS JALAHALLI, BENGALURU (EAST). 19.3. AFS TAMBARAM, CHENNAI. 19.4. MTTI, AFS AVADI. . 22.
